name: Active-Capital Value-Creation Plan

positioning.oneLineSummary: Turns investor value-add from reputation into named, capacity-backed actions linked to company milestones.
positioning.productLabel: Active-Capital Pattern — derived from Mallaby's public venture history

attribution.display: Historical pattern derived from Sebastian Mallaby's public materials, qualified by contract research

neutralParaphrase: If investor involvement is part of the thesis, specify the milestone, action, responsible partner, resource, timing, and evidence of capacity. Evaluate governance and terms for both company value and investor value; more control is not automatically better.

locator.value: Table of contents, chapters on activist capital and firm models
Transcript discussion of investors working with founders, boards, networks, and team responsibility
Abstract on VC value creation, bargaining power, and terms that can reduce startup value

requiredConditions: The fund claims an active role in the company.
Investor capacity and relevant capability are observable.
Company and investor objectives and conflicts remain separate.

requiredEvidence.description: Milestone, action, owner, resource, date, expected evidence, and fallback.
Partner time, portfolio load, specialist availability, and demonstrated relevant capability.
Founder agreement, governance rights, incentives, and possible conflicts.

decisionQuestions: Which company bottleneck can this investor causally improve?
Who will act, with what resource and capacity?
Do proposed terms improve company outcomes or mainly transfer value?
positiveSignals: Actions match a verified company bottleneck.
A named partner has time and relevant evidence of capability.
Founder and investor agree on role and escalation.
Impact is observable without claiming sole causality.
redFlags: Value-add is a list of generic platform services.
No responsible person or time allocation exists.
Control terms are called support without company-value analysis.
Past brand reputation substitutes for current capacity.
disconfirmingEvidence: Founder does not want or need the proposed intervention.
Terms lower startup success probability or future financing flexibility.
A third party can provide the same resource at lower cost.
contraindications: Do not attribute company success solely to investor activity.
Do not assume stronger control maximizes joint value.
Do not score brand without an executable plan.

instructions: Specify investor action, owner, resource, and capacity.
Test founder alignment and governance tradeoffs.
Conclude executable value plan, generic support, conflict, or no active role.

sourceReliability.medium: Named plan and some prior evidence.
sourceReliability.high: Capacity records, founder agreement, and relevant prior outcomes support the plan.

evidenceStrength.medium: Specific action exists but impact or capacity is uncertain.
evidenceStrength.high: Bottleneck, action, capacity, alignment, and observation are explicit.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Action and owner covered; alignment or tradeoff partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Bottleneck, action, owner, resource, capacity, alignment, governance, and milestone complete.

applicabilityConfidence.low: Passive investment or no identified bottleneck.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Active role is material to the thesis and contract.

judgmentConfidence.high: An executable, aligned, capacity-backed value plan is supported.

empiricalQualifications: Contract terms can benefit investors while reducing startup value.

rights.notes: Historical patterns are paraphrased; the execution plan is product synthesis.

openIssues: Define a non-self-serving method for tracking investor contribution.
